issue: Does a prior state drug conviction qualify as a 'controlled substance' offense under the career offender guideline when the state's definition covers a substance, such as hemp, that is not controlled under federal law?

sides.position: A state drug conviction qualifies only if the substance is controlled under federal law (federally based approach).
cases: United States v. Townsend, 897 F.3d 66 (2d Cir. 2018)
United States v. Gomez-Alvarez, 781 F.3d 787 (5th Cir. 2015)
United States v. Bautista, 989 F.3d 698 (9th Cir. 2021)
United States v. Crocco, 15 F.4th 20 (1st Cir. 2021)
United States v. Fulcar, No. 24-1524 (1st Cir. 2026)

sides.position: A state drug conviction can qualify if the state law defines the controlled substance more broadly than federal law (state-law approach).

this_court: The First Circuit adopts the federally based approach, joining the side of the split held by the Second, Fifth, and Ninth Circuits.
quote: We join the latter half of this circuit split for the reasons we will next explain.
cite: United States v. Fulcar, No. 24-1524 (1st Cir. 2026)
